random0: There's a saying that no news is good news. You have come to appreciate it since the siege began. Today the guns are quiet. Men sleep beside their posts, shops open their shutters, and for a few hours the City remembers what an ordinary day felt like.
random1: A hundred infantrymen and fifty archers have abandoned their posts for the monasteries. Some claim they have come to pray. Others have hidden their weapons and refuse to leave. If sanctuary becomes a way to escape the walls, more men will follow them. How shall we bring them back?
random2: Bread prices have risen again. In the Merchant Quarter, a crowd overturns a stall and demands that the Emperor make the merchants sell at a fair price. Shopkeepers bolt their doors. The City needs both its hungry people and the men who keep its markets supplied.
random3: Rain sweeps across the harbour and thunder drowns the guns. Ottoman watch-fires disappear behind the downpour. The storm offers cover for a raid, if our own men can find their way home. It also offers something the garrison has almost forgotten: a night of rest.
random4: A rumour travels through the alehouses: the Sultan offered generous terms, but the Emperor rejected them out of greed and a hunger for glory. Your agents believe Ottoman spies are paying men to repeat it. By morning, the tale has reached the barracks. How shall we answer it?
random5: One of our cannon bursts as it fires. The crew scatters beneath a cloud of burnt powder; broken metal rings against the stone. Men from the neighbouring battery refuse to load their gun until someone explains what happened. Christ protect us…
random6: After dark, crowds gather with candles outside the churches. Priests lead prayers for the City while soldiers listen from the walls. Some workers have left their shifts to join the vigils. The people need hope. Your foremen need hands.
random7: A guard catches a hungry man breaking into a food warehouse. The thief says his children have eaten nothing since yesterday. By noon half the neighbourhood has gathered outside the guardhouse, and the case has reached the Emperor. Everyone will hear what sentence you give.
random9: A poet has drawn a crowd in the Grand Market. His verses praise the people who keep the City alive. They also make several pointed observations about their Emperor. You hear that the best of these have already reached the barracks. What shall we do with him?
random10: Citizens arrive at the damaged walls carrying stone, timber and their own tools. The guards make room for them. Men who yesterday complained about the cannon are now helping to repair its damage. Their stubbornness lifts the garrison's spirits.
random11: Someone at an alehouse has heard that the Hungarian king is gathering an army. Someone else knows a man whose cousin has seen the sails of a Western fleet. By evening, half the City expects reinforcements. Your envoys have sent no such report. Nonetheless, the rumour spreads…
random12: Someone at an alehouse declares that our allies have abandoned us. The story grows with every telling: the fleets have turned back, the kings have refused, the Pope has forgotten the City. Your envoys have confirmed none of it. Nonetheless, the rumour spreads…
random13: The war council proposes a raid on the Ottoman camp. The enemy believes us cornered behind the walls; a sudden attack might burn supplies, kill gunners or draw men into an ambush. The council's enthusiasm grows until someone asks who will lead it. How shall we proceed?
random14: Guards find long cracks in the outer wall. One swears they were smaller yesterday. The masons disagree about how far they run through the stone. A surface flaw might be harmless; a weak foundation could give the enemy a breach. We must decide before the guns resume.
random15: Loukas Notaras reports a suspected traitor among the palace servants. Your network has {GetInt("iSpies")} spies, and several have noticed the man leaving at night. He returns before dawn and gives different accounts of where he has been. Notaras asks whether to investigate, arrest him or make him disappear.
random16: A noble of the Doukas family throws himself from a palace tower, splattering his brains across half the street below. Some blame a rejected courtship; others whisper that even the aristocracy has lost hope of surviving the siege. His family wants the death called an accident. The priests want to know whether he may receive Christian burial. The City is already telling its own version.
random17: An Ottoman cannon explodes as its crew prepares to fire. From the wall you see smoke, broken timber and men running among the fallen. Our lookouts confirm that the gun is destroyed. For once, the noise from the enemy camp is welcome.
random19: Fire breaks out near the Phanar docks. The wind carries sparks from roof to roof, and a warehouse keeper is trying to drag his stock into the street. Bells summon help. Someone must organise it before the whole quarter burns.
random20: An engineer slips from a ladder while repairing the walls. The men beneath him can do nothing. By the time his foreman reaches him, he is dead. The foreman brings you his name and asks what should be sent to his family.
random21: The storekeeper opens a barrel and finds mould beneath the top layer of grain. Several more are the same. He asks whether to burn the spoiled food or try to salvage it. Today that seems a question for a cook. Soon it may be a question for the Emperor.
random22: Quarrels break out in the barracks. Men complain about the rations, their cramped quarters and the officers who always seem to eat better. Yesterday two sentries traded blows over a blanket. Your captains ask for something to distract the men before the next quarrel becomes a mutiny.
